parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, no documented police targeting, no universal-exposure measure (no facility ban, no entry-screening or marker rule documented), and a constitutional equality guarantee since 2018 — though whether gender identity is enumerated is unresolved and no enforcement record exists. The negative inputs are thin and dated: a 2015 societal-stigma finding predating the reform, an untested guarantee, and open questions (custody placement, document practice, emergency care) which count as questions, not exposures. Missing legal gender recognition is a resident gap, not visitor-facing. No trans-specific violence data exists — absence of evidence, not safety, but nothing documents a campaign either. Thin-data extrapolation from non-criminalisation plus equality framing points to reduced rather than elevated risk, while documented stigma and unproven protections keep it below the acceptance-with-working-protections tier.
